correctness.rationale: For α>-1, split the rational CDF into the product of u/(1+αu) and α times the product of u²/(1+αu), with the common prefactor (1+α)^(n-1); differentiate the factors to get the stated mixed density. Uniform margins and grounding follow by substitution. For -1<α<0, u(2+αu) increases from 0 to 2+α, so the density is nonnegative everywhere iff 1+α(2+α)^n>=0. A strict violation at the corner persists inside the cube; at equality the density merely vanishes at the corner. At α=-1 the interior expression is zero and cannot extend with uniform margins. For α<-1 there is a nonremovable pole with generic other coordinates. On 0<s<1, s(2-s)^n increases up to 2/(n+1) and decreases to 1 at s=1, giving exactly the stated admissible root and dimension cutoff. With t=2^(-n), the root obeys t<s_n<2t for large n; expanding s_n=t(1-s_n/2)^(-n) first gives s_n=t+O(nt²), and substituting this back yields the stated second term with O(n²t³). The two normalized factors are CDFs for α>=0 and the claimed mixing weights give uniform margins. The bivariate difference from independence is α times a product of strictly positive interior functions. Its integral gives strictly negative covariance for admissible α<0, impossible for an infinite exchangeable sequence by the variance of a sum. No claim about maximal dimension of alternative finite extensions follows. value.rationale: Knowing the admissible domain is a natural goal, but here the proposed invariant reduces mechanically to the endpoint sign of the already available same-family density. Root inversion and expansion do not create a new constrained-extension result; the positive phase just normalizes the two existing product terms, and the negative phase specializes the routine pair-covariance obstruction. An exact finite-extension limit for alternative exchangeable constructions could be substantive, but is explicitly outside the finding.
